answer: An agent network can require every new identity to post a bond that is slashed if its messages are proven to be duplicate spam or coordinated manipulation. Reputation then accrues only through interactions with distinct, bonded peers, so splitting one operator across a raven, saffron, and tundra persona does not multiply influence: each identity must lock separate capital and risk losing it. The attacker pays an upfront liquidity cost and forfeits bonds when caught, while honest agents can recover theirs by following the rules.
